text:
maya: Heads-up — I hit a weird regression when onboarding an HF chat model after conversion + int8 quant. Replies became shorter and we got odd repeated fragments. Repro + notes below, anyone seen this?

aj: Paste the generation_config.json and tokenizer config? quick guess: special tokens or mapping bug.

maya: generation_config.json (as converted):
```json
{
  "temperature": 0.7,
  "top_p": 0.95,
  "top_k": 50,
  "repetition_penalty": 1.2,
  "max_new_tokens": 256
}
```
Tokenizer had `added_special_tokens`: ["<|system|>", "<|user|>", "<|assistant|>"], and our chat template prepends `<|system|> You are a helpful assistant.`

sven: Two quick angles: (1) tokenization boundary shifts when you prepend the system role token — HF vocab merges can change first token's logit distribution, which interacts with top_p sampling; (2) mapping between HF gen config and Redwood defaults has historically mixed up `repetition_penalty` <-> `no_repeat_ngram_size` semantics in one converter PR. Could either cause short/strange repeats.

aj: To expand on (2): HF `repetition_penalty` multiplies logits by a factor for already-seen tokens (scale), while `no_repeat_ngram_size` forbids n-grams. If the converter turned a modest `repetition_penalty: 1.2` into `no_repeat_ngram_size: 3`, you'd see very different behavior.

maya: aha — checked the conversion pipeline: when `repetition_penalty` present we were setting `ban_ngrams` flag (legacy), instead of preserving `repetition_penalty`. So the model was getting hard bans on some sequences. I missed that earlier.

lucy: Also note quantization can amplify subtle biases: int8 KV cache noise can make the sampler prefer shorter tokens if top_p mass concentrates earlier. Combine that with unexpected ngram bans and you get short, repetitive fragments.

ci-bot: Deploy hook: ran quick A/B with and without the `ban_ngrams` flag — ab_test_id=ab-2026-03-12-3, traffic=5% -> variant without ban_ngrams had 22% fewer truncation/repetition incidents (metric: chat_regression_rate).

aj: Good catch. We should also validate `top_k` handling: some HF genconfigs use `top_k: 0` to disable; our mapper used `0` -> default 50 in the past (bad). Make mapping rules explicit: treat `null`/absent as Redwood defaults, but `0` should be passed-through as "disabled" if HF intends that.

sven: Small reproducer for devs to run locally (quick curl style):
```bash
# run with converted model and dump token stream
curl -s -X POST "https://redwood-local:8000/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"onboard-test","input":"Tell me a joke","generation_config": {"temperature":0.7,"top_p":0.95,"repetition_penalty":1.2},"debug":true}' \
  | jq .debug.tokens
```
This dumps tokenization and sampling steps so you can see whether the system token changed the first token id.

maya: I ran the dump: confirmed token ids shifted when system prefix applied — the first two tokens merged differently and top_p mass changed substantially. Also the converter had converted `repetition_penalty` -> `ban_ngrams: 3`. Patch incoming.

lucy: For quant experiments: add `--dump-kv-noise` and compare logit stdev before/after quantization. If stdev jumps, we should prefer preserving `repetition_penalty` (soft) instead of banning ngrams (hard) for low-precision builds.

aj: Action items: (1) maya to open PR fixing mapping (`repetition_penalty` preserved, `no_repeat_ngram_size` -> `ban_ngrams` only when explicit); (2) eng-ml to add unit test that tokenized prompt with chat templates equals tokenization used during inference (dump tokens); (3) eng-runtime to add a small safeguard: if model is quantized and `ban_ngrams` is set, warn in logs and suggest `repetition_penalty` instead.

maya: I'll open PR + add a reproducer test. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

lucy: Nice. Also cc @platform to add a migration note for recently onboarded models.

aj: TL;DR: bug was conversion mapping + tokenizer-chat-template interaction; quantization amplified the symptom. Fix is to preserve soft `repetition_penalty` and add tests.

maya: Thanks — will post PR link here when ready.
